handbook.title: The IoT Engineering Handbook
handbook.subtitle: Standards, architectures and the foundations of connected systems
handbook.description: Study IoT definitions, reference architectures, information flows, interoperability, reliability, security and device lifecycle through standards-grounded explanations.
handbook.intro: A standards-grounded handbook for software engineers studying connected systems. Begin with definitions and reference models, then reason about sensing, communication, control, deployment and lifecycle. Conceptual diagrams and worked examples support the reading.

chapters.title: What Is an IoT System?
chapters.subtitle: Definitions, reference models and engineering responsibilities
chapters.description: Understand IoT through standard models, sensing and control flows, deployment choices, interoperability, reliability, security and lifecycle.
chapters.outcome: you can explain an IoT system’s functions, deployment, information flows and lifecycle responsibilities.
chapters.prerequisiteText: Familiarity with software components, network requests and distributed-system failure. No electronics or hardware required.

chapters.title: Sensors and the Physical World
chapters.subtitle: Measurement chains, sensing principles and decision-ready results
chapters.description: Trace a sensor reading from physical coupling to a software result. Study calibration, sampling, sensor lag and uncertainty through worked examples.
chapters.outcome: you can judge whether a sensor reading supports a physical-world decision.

chapters.title: Boards — From Prototypes to Industrial Systems
chapters.subtitle: Firmware, interfaces and the constraints behind board selection
chapters.description: Follow a sensor reading through firmware and Bluetooth. Compare boards using memory, timing, energy, interfaces and recovery requirements.
chapters.outcome: you can trace firmware execution and compare board architectures against explicit deployment requirements.

chapters.title: Firmware, Clocks, and Timing
chapters.subtitle: Execution, clock domains and the timing contracts behind reliable firmware
chapters.description: Trace firmware from reset to acquisition and communication. Reason about scheduling, clock synchronization, drift, sleep and recovery.
chapters.outcome: you can define firmware execution and timestamp contracts through clock correction, sleep and reset.

requiredSections: If You Only Read One Section
